section-navy6.h2: Missing teeth change more than your smile.
section-navy6.text: They change what you eat, how you speak, and the shape of your jaw. Teeth shift into the gap, dentures need adhesive to stay put, and missing roots let the jawbone recede. Implants fuse to the bone and stop that drift.

section7.h2: One surgeon, every phase of your case.
section7.benefit-text: Posts are placed using fully guided All-on-X technique, planned on your scan before surgery rather than judged in the chair.
section7.benefit-text2: Planning happens digitally on a 3D scan, so the position of every implant is decided before the day of surgery.
section7.benefit-text3: Dr. Bennett is board certified to administer IV sedation and does so himself. Most implant patients here choose it.
section7.benefit-text4: Consultation, surgery, sedation and the lab work happen under one roof, so you are not handed between offices halfway through.

section9.h32: Placement, with sedation if you want it

section10.h2: Every phase of your case, one surgeon.

section10.text2: A University of Iowa dental graduate, he has placed and restored thousands of implants, and is recognized as a Top Dentist by 5280 Magazine.

section13.faq-toggle: Am I too old for dental implants?
section13.faq-answer: Age on its own is rarely the deciding factor — bone volume and general health matter far more. That is exactly what the 3D scan at your free consultation is for, and Dr. Bennett will tell you plainly if implants are not the right route for you.
section13.faq-answer2: Dr. Bennett is board certified to administer IV sedation and does so himself. Most implant patients at the practice choose it, and the procedure is carried out with you fully comfortable.
section13.faq-toggle3: How long does the whole thing take?
section13.faq-answer3: It depends on the case. Full-arch patients frequently leave with fixed teeth on the day of surgery, then return for the final restoration once the implants have integrated with the bone. Single-tooth cases follow the same pattern over a shorter span.
section13.faq-answer4: The practice works with most dental insurance, but does not accept HMO or Medicaid plans. Monthly payment plans are available if you would rather spread the cost — the patient coordinator will go through the options with you.
